result:
I changed the upstream-proxy CONNECT authority to bracket IPv6 literals, so a request for `::1` port 443 now goes out as `CONNECT [::1]:443` instead of `CONNECT ::1:443`. I didn't run any tests, and I didn't add one.

The change is in `HttpUpstreamProxy.start_handshake` in `mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/_upstream_proxy.py`. It checks whether the target host parses as an IPv6 address. If so, it wraps the host in brackets. Otherwise it encodes the host with `idna` as before. The `Host` header uses the same authority, so it is bracketed too when `http_connect_send_host_header` is on.

I skipped a test because the existing CONNECT tests in `test/mitmproxy/proxy/layers/http/test_http.py` have their own setup that I didn't want to guess at. A natural addition would be a copy of the one around line 747 with an IPv6 target, expecting `CONNECT [::1]:443 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [::1]:443\r\n\r\n`.
